title: Singulion Structure and the Voynich Manuscript
authors: Colin Layfield and Lisa Fagin Davis
summary: The authors use latent semantic analysis to compare text on the two sides of one leaf, across the fold of one bifolium, and across facing pages in the current binding. They use the Aberdeen Bestiary and Speculum Humanae Salvationis as controls and test a proposed arrangement of the manuscript as individual folded sheets.
established: In the two benchmark manuscripts, present facing pages and consecutive sides of the same leaf show similar text similarity, while the across-fold comparisons tend to be lower. In MS 408, across-fold scores are closer to scores for the same leaf, and present facing-page scores are lower.

An exhaustive search within the balneological and marginal-stars sections found hypothetical bifolium orders with higher average facing-page similarity than the existing binding. The paper also points to initial-glyph features on f76r and f105r as independent codicological support for features of those proposals.

open.question: Do physical or graphic clues independent of the fitted text-similarity score support the proposed bifolium sequences across the manuscript?
open.check: Compare candidate arrangements against recorded ruling, image continuation, scribal openings and other evidence from the scans. Include competing arrangements and record where several sequences fit.
